reviews.text: Mehn, the jollof rice here is on point! Smoky, well-seasoned and the portion is generous. Service was a bit slow but the food made up for it. I'll definitely come back.
Solid breakfast spot. Their pancakes are fluffy and the akara is crispy outside, soft inside. A bit pricey but worth it for a weekend treat.
The vibe is great, music was nice but the food was just okay. Their pasta needs more flavour, abeg. I'd come back for drinks though.
Quick, affordable Nigerian food. The amala and ewedu hits different when you're hungry after work. Sitting space is small but the food delivers.
Love this place. The egusi soup is rich and authentic, plus you get culture and art on the side. Easily one of my favourite spots in VI.
Good coffee, reliable WiFi, comfortable for working. Their chicken sandwich is decent. Gets crowded on weekends so come early.
Nice ambience and the view of the beach is amazing. Food is overpriced for what you get, but the experience is decent for a date night.
Best Indian food in Lagos, hands down. The butter chicken is creamy and full of flavour. Their naan is fresh. Service was attentive.
Long queues at checkout almost every time. Selection is okay but the experience can be frustrating. They need more cashiers, on God.
Fast service. The fried rice and chicken combo never disappoints. Affordable and filling.
Vibes were crazy! Suya was peppery just how I like it, drinks flowed all night. Best Friday night I've had in a minute.
Pizza was alright. Delivery took longer than expected. Cheese could be more generous for the price sef.
Authentic afang soup that reminds me of home. Owner is super warm. Will recommend to anyone who wants real Nigerian flavours.
Their ice cream is creamy and the waffles are great. A bit small space-wise but cosy. Good for a quick date.
